note: B adds thirteen further claims that are correct and well bound — equipment manufacturer (DRYER/BLOMBERG), finish data (ACCENT PAINT colour number 33-14, WALL BASE profile), and furniture/millwork quantities tied to the right tags (F2–F6, MWK02, MWK04, MWK05, MWB01, MWK03) — while A omits all of them. Both sets share the same seven defective claims caused by splicing across schedule rows (e.g. dryer model DV17540NBL00 credited to PRATT & LAMBERT, P3 given type TEMPERED, KITCHEN given colour name STEEL WOOL, SHOWER SURROUND given colour number 33-14, and QUARTZ given an invented location KITCHEN). Error rates are therefore equal, but B covers far more of the page's engineering content, so B is the better set.
remarks: The text layer lists schedule tags in blocks separate from their rows, which is the likely source of the cross-row splicing seen in both sets (paint manufacturer attached to a dryer model, glass type attached to tag P3, paint colour attached to locations KITCHEN/SHOWER SURROUND). The GL (Glass) type=Tempered claim is factually right but its quote ('LOCATION: BATHROOM SHOWER P3 TYPE: TEMPERED') does not support it; the same tempered-glass fact is also stated under the wrong name P3, and the accent-paint colour 33-14 appears under both ACCENT PAINT and SHOWER SURROUND. 'FINISH' is an attribute label used as an entity, and 'F2' is ambiguous because tag F2 exists in both the furniture (bedside table) and plumbing (kitchen faucet) schedules. Both sets still leave out many schedule facts: appliance/plumbing models, TV size 40", glass thickness 1/2", tile and laminate dimensions, and wall base location/finish.
